title: PHP core use-after-free / stale request state - unauthenticated RCE

distro_frozen_versions._note: Version strings distributions ship unchanged for the life of a release and patch by backport. A banner showing one of these is not evidence of vulnerability on its own.

8.0.30._why: 8.0.30 is also the final upstream 8.0 release: without a distro hint it is treated as vanilla EOL

evidence: Ubuntu 24.04: php8.3 8.3.6-0ubuntu0.24.04.13 (noble-security) changelog lists CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 while PHP_VERSION stays 8.3.6 (observed 2026-10-22).

distro_branches._note: PHP branches each distribution family ships in its own packages. A Server header naming the distribution only hints at a backport when the disclosed branch is one it ships; otherwise the PHP was built from upstream (e.g. the official php Docker images report Apache '(Debian)' with PHP 8.3/8.5). Families not listed (RHEL and clones ship many branches through module streams, SUSE, Fedora) always count as a hint.

_oracle_note: --oracle is only valid for this advisory: it reads the session-write warning that THIS fix removed. A new advisory must not set 'oracle' unless its fix has a validated behavioural difference.

cvss3_by_cve._source: NVD primary CVSS 3.1 (nvd@nist.gov, status Analyzed), read from services.nvd.nist.gov on 2026-10-23. cvss3_vector/cvss3_score above = the higher of the two, used for the combined finding.
